name: Bukit Timah
summary: Tree canopy, school corridors, and family housing — the classic west-central expat belt for drivers and school-run households, with premium rents street-by-street.
body: Bukit Timah is less a single village and more a corridor of green, schools, and landed/condo pockets stretching toward Upper Bukit Timah, Sixth Avenue, and the Botanic Gardens fringe. Families shortlist it for proximity to international campuses (and the social network that forms at school gates) plus a calmer evening rhythm than Holland V nightlife or River Valley density. Forum “where would you live” threads still put Bukit Timah in the premium family shortlist alongside Tanglin — useful when school waitlists and bus routes dominate the housing thesis. Walkability varies block by block — many households become de facto car or Grab households even with Downtown Line access at Sixth Avenue / Tan Kah Kee. Nature Reserve trails matter if weekends outdoors are non-negotiable. Compare rents street-by-street: a two-block shift can mean a four-figure monthly swing. Club shortlists often include Hollandse Club and Tanglin-side options; American Club is a drive, not a stroll, from many Bukit Timah addresses. Ops notes for renters: visitor parking rules at condo lobbies, mould risk in leafy older stock, and fibre installs that still need landlord access windows on landed plots.
watchOuts: Less walkable grocery density than Katong strips
housingMix: Landed, townhouses, and mid-to-large family condos.
commuteNotes: Downtown Line (Sixth Avenue, Tan Kah Kee); buses along Bukit Timah Road; Botanic Gardens interchange nearby.
